617|/* Start a new instruction bundle.  Returns the rs_align_code frag that
618|   will be used to align the new bundle.  */
619|static fragS *
620|start_bundle (void)
621|{
622|  fragS *frag = frag_now;
623|
624|  frag_align_code (0, 0);
625|
626|  while (frag->fr_type != rs_align_code)
627|    frag = frag->fr_next;
628|
629|  gas_assert (frag != frag_now);
630|
631|  return frag;
632|}
633|
634|/* Calculate the maximum size after relaxation of the region starting
635|   at the given frag and extending through frag_now (which is unfinished).  */
636|static unsigned int
637|pending_bundle_size (fragS *frag)
638|{
639|  unsigned int offset = frag->fr_fix;
640|  unsigned int size = 0;
641|
642|  gas_assert (frag != frag_now);
643|  gas_assert (frag->fr_type == rs_align_code);
644|
645|  while (frag != frag_now)
646|    {
647|      /* This should only happen in what will later become an error case.  */
648|      if (frag == NULL)
649|	return 0;
650|
651|      size += frag->fr_fix;
652|      if (frag->fr_type == rs_machine_dependent)
653|	size += md_frag_max_var (frag);
654|
655|      frag = frag->fr_next;
656|    }
657|
658|  gas_assert (frag == frag_now);
659|  size += frag_now_fix ();
660|  if (frag->fr_type == rs_machine_dependent)
661|    size += md_frag_max_var (frag);
662|
663|  gas_assert (size >= offset);
664|
665|  return size - offset;
666|}

668|/* Finish off the frag created to ensure bundle alignment.  */
669|static void
670|finish_bundle (fragS *frag, unsigned int size)
671|{
672|  gas_assert (bundle_align_p2 > 0);
673|  gas_assert (frag->fr_type == rs_align_code);
674|
675|  if (size > 1)
676|    {
677|      /* If there is more than a single byte, then we need to set up the
678|	 alignment frag.  Otherwise we leave it at its initial state from
679|	 calling frag_align_code (0, 0), so that it does nothing.  */
680|      frag->fr_offset = bundle_align_p2;
681|      frag->fr_subtype = size - 1;
682|    }
683|
684|  /* We do this every time rather than just in s_bundle_align_mode
685|     so that we catch any affected section without needing hooks all
686|     over for all paths that do section changes.  It's cheap enough.  */
687|  if (bundle_align_p2 > OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER)

741|{

744|  return (flags & SEC_ALLOC) && !(flags & (SEC_LOAD | SEC_HAS_CONTENTS));

747|/* Guts of .align directive:
748|   N is the power of two to which to align.  A value of zero is accepted but
749|    ignored: the default alignment of the section will be at least this.
750|   FILL may be NULL, or it may point to the bytes of the fill pattern.
751|   LEN is the length of whatever FILL points to, if anything.  If LEN is zero
752|    but FILL is not NULL then LEN is treated as if it were one.
753|   MAX is the maximum number of characters to skip when doing the alignment,
754|    or 0 if there is no maximum.  */
755|
756|void
757|do_align (unsigned int n, char *fill, unsigned int len, unsigned int max)
758|{
759|  if (now_seg == absolute_section || in_bss ())
760|    {
761|      if (fill != NULL)
762|	while (len-- > 0)
763|	  if (*fill++ != '\0')
764|	    {
765|	      if (now_seg == absolute_section)
766|		as_warn (_("ignoring fill value in absolute section"));
767|	      else
768|		as_warn (_("ignoring fill value in section `%s'"),
769|			 segment_name (now_seg));
770|	      break;
771|	    }
772|      fill = NULL;
773|      len = 0;
774|    }
775|
776|#ifdef md_flush_pending_output
777|  md_flush_pending_output ();
778|#endif
779|
780|#ifdef md_do_align
781|  md_do_align (n, fill, len, max, just_record_alignment);
782|#endif
783|
784|  /* Only make a frag if we HAVE to...  */
785|  if ((n > OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER) && !need_pass_2)
786|    {
787|      if (fill == NULL)
788|	{
789|	  if (subseg_text_p (now_seg))
790|	    frag_align_code (n, max);
791|	  else
792|	    frag_align (n, 0, max);
793|	}
794|      else if (len <= 1)
795|	frag_align (n, *fill, max);
796|      else
797|	frag_align_pattern (n, fill, len, max);
798|    }
799|
800|#ifdef md_do_align
801| just_record_alignment: ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_LABEL
802|#endif
803|
804|  if (n > OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER)
805|    record_alignment (now_seg, n - OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER);

1342|/* Convert O_constant expression EXP into the equivalent O_big representation.
1343|   Take the sign of the number from SIGN rather than X_add_number.  */
1344|
1345|static void
1346|convert_to_bignum (expressionS *exp, int sign)
1347|{
1348|  valueT value;
1349|  unsigned int i;
1350|
1351|  value = exp->X_add_number;
1352|  for (i = 0; i < sizeof (exp->X_add_number) / CHARS_PER_LITTLENUM; i++)
1353|    {
1354|      generic_bignum[i] = value & LITTLENUM_MASK;
1355|      value >>= LITTLENUM_NUMBER_OF_BITS;
1356|    }
1357|  /* Add a sequence of sign bits if the top bit of X_add_number is not
1358|     the sign of the original value.  */
1359|  if ((exp->X_add_number < 0) == !sign)
1360|    generic_bignum[i++] = sign ? LITTLENUM_MASK : 0;
1361|  exp->X_op = O_big;
1362|  exp->X_add_number = i;

1421|/* Handle the .align pseudo-op.  A positive ARG is a default alignment
1422|   (in bytes).  A negative ARG is the negative of the length of the
1423|   fill pattern.  BYTES_P is non-zero if the alignment value should be
1424|   interpreted as the byte boundary, rather than the power of 2.  */
1425|#ifndef TC_ALIGN_LIMIT
1426|#define TC_ALIGN_LIMIT (stdoutput->arch_info->bits_per_address - 1)
1427|#endif
1428|
1429|static void
1430|s_align (signed int arg, int bytes_p)
1431|{
1432|  unsigned int align_limit = TC_ALIGN_LIMIT;
1433|  addressT align;
1434|  char *stop = NULL;
1435|  char stopc = 0;
1436|  offsetT fill = 0;
1437|  unsigned int max;
1438|  int fill_p;
1439|
1440|  if (flag_mri)
1441|    stop = mri_comment_field (&stopc);
1442|
1443|  if (is_end_of_line[(unsigned char) *input_line_pointer])
1444|    {
1445|      if (arg < 0)
1446|	align = 0;
1447|      else
1448|	align = arg;	/* Default value from pseudo-op table.  */
1449|    }
1450|  else
1451|    {
1452|      align = get_absolute_expression ();
1453|      SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1454|
1455|#ifdef TC_ALIGN_ZERO_IS_DEFAULT
1456|      if (arg > 0 && align == 0)
1457|	align = arg;
1458|#endif
1459|    }
1460|
1461|  if (bytes_p)
1462|    {
1463|      /* Convert to a power of 2.  */
1464|      if (align != 0)
1465|	{
1466|	  unsigned int i;
1467|
1468|	  for (i = 0; (align & 1) == 0; align >>= 1, ++i)
1469|	    ;
1470|	  if (align != 1)
1471|	    as_bad (_("alignment not a power of 2"));
1472|
1473|	  align = i;
1474|	}
1475|    }
1476|
1477|  if (align > align_limit)
1478|    {
1479|      align = align_limit;
1480|      as_warn (_("alignment too large: %u assumed"), align_limit);
1481|    }
1482|
1483|  if (*input_line_pointer != ',')
1484|    {
1485|      fill_p = 0;
1486|      max = 0;
1487|    }
1488|  else
1489|    {
1490|      ++input_line_pointer;
1491|      if (*input_line_pointer == ',')
1492|	fill_p = 0;
1493|      else
1494|	{
1495|	  fill = get_absolute_expression ();
1496|	  SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1497|	  fill_p = 1;
1498|	}
1499|
1500|      if (*input_line_pointer != ',')
1501|	max = 0;
1502|      else
1503|	{
1504|	  ++input_line_pointer;
1505|	  max = get_absolute_expression ();
1506|	}
1507|    }
1508|
1509|  if (!fill_p)
1510|    {
1511|      if (arg < 0)
1512|	as_warn (_("expected fill pattern missing"));
1513|      do_align (align, (char *) NULL, 0, max);
1514|    }
1515|  else
1516|    {
1517|      unsigned int fill_len;
1518|
1519|      if (arg >= 0)
1520|	fill_len = 1;
1521|      else
1522|	fill_len = -arg;
1523|
1524|      if (fill_len <= 1)
1525|	{
1526|	  char fill_char = 0;
1527|
1528|	  fill_char = fill;
1529|	  do_align (align, &fill_char, fill_len, max);
1530|	}
1531|      else
1532|	{
1533|	  char ab[16];
1534|
1535|	  if ((size_t) fill_len > sizeof ab)
1536|	    {
1537|	      as_warn (_("fill pattern too long, truncating to %u"),
1538|		       (unsigned) sizeof ab);
1539|	      fill_len = sizeof ab;
1540|	    }
1541|
1542|	  md_number_to_chars (ab, fill, fill_len);
1543|	  do_align (align, ab, fill_len, max);
1544|	}
1545|    }
1546|
1547|  demand_empty_rest_of_line ();
1548|
1549|  if (flag_mri)
1550|    mri_comment_end (stop, stopc);
1551|}

1580|/* Read a symbol name from input_line_pointer.
1581|
1582|   Stores the symbol name in a buffer and returns a pointer to this buffer.
1583|   The buffer is xalloc'ed.  It is the caller's responsibility to free
1584|   this buffer.
1585|
1586|   The name is not left in the i_l_p buffer as it may need processing
1587|   to handle escape characters.
1588|
1589|   Advances i_l_p to the next non-whitespace character.
1590|
1591|   If a symbol name could not be read, the routine issues an error
1592|   messages, skips to the end of the line and returns NULL.  */
1593|
1594|char *
1595|read_symbol_name (void)
1596|{
1597|  char * name;
1598|  char * start;
1599|  char c;
1600|
1601|  c = *input_line_pointer++;
1602|
1603|  if (c == '"')
1604|    {
1605|#define SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN 128
1606|      ptrdiff_t len = SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN;
1607|      char * name_end;
1608|      unsigned int C;
1609|
1610|      start = name = XNEWVEC (char, len + 1);
1611|
1612|      name_end = name + SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN;
1613|
1614|      while (is_a_char (C = next_char_of_string ()))
1615|	{
1616|	  if (name >= name_end)
1617|	    {
1618|	      ptrdiff_t sofar;
1619|
1620|	      sofar = name - start;
1621|	      len += SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN;
1622|	      start = XRESIZEVEC (char, start, len + 1);
1623|	      name_end = start + len;
1624|	      name = start + sofar;
1625|	    }
1626|
1627|	  *name++ = (char) C;
1628|	}
1629|      *name = 0;
1630|
1631|      /* Since quoted symbol names can contain non-ASCII characters,
1632|	 check the string and warn if it cannot be recognised by the
1633|	 current character set.  */
1634|      if (mbstowcs (NULL, name, len) == (size_t) -1)
1635|	as_warn (_("symbol name not recognised in the current locale"));
1636|    }
1637|  else if (is_name_beginner (c) || (input_from_string && c == FAKE_LABEL_CHAR))
1638|    {
1639|      ptrdiff_t len;
1640|
1641|      name = input_line_pointer - 1;
1642|
1643|      /* We accept FAKE_LABEL_CHAR in a name in case this is
1644|	 being called with a constructed string.  */
1645|      while (is_part_of_name (c = *input_line_pointer++)
1646|	     || (input_from_string && c == FAKE_LABEL_CHAR))
1647|	;
1648|
1649|      len = (input_line_pointer - name) - 1;
1650|      start = XNEWVEC (char, len + 1);
1651|
1652|      memcpy (start, name, len);
1653|      start[len] = 0;
1654|
1655|      /* Skip a name ender char if one is present.  */
1656|      if (! is_name_ender (c))
1657|	--input_line_pointer;
1658|    }
1659|  else
1660|    name = start = NULL;
1661|
1662|  if (name == start)
1663|    {
1664|      as_bad (_("expected symbol name"));
1665|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1666|      free (start);
1667|      return NULL;
1668|    }
1669|
1670|  SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1671|
1672|  return start;
1673|}

1676|symbolS *
1677|s_comm_internal (int param,
1678|		 symbolS *(*comm_parse_extra) (int, symbolS *, addressT))
1679|{
1680|  char *name;
1681|  offsetT temp, size;
1682|  symbolS *symbolP = NULL;
1683|  char *stop = NULL;
1684|  char stopc = 0;
1685|  expressionS exp;
1686|
1687|  if (flag_mri)
1688|    stop = mri_comment_field (&stopc);

1694|     required, but Irix 5 cc does not generate it for .lcomm.  */
1695|  if (*input_line_pointer == ',')
1696|    input_line_pointer++;
1697|
1698|  temp = get_absolute_expr (&exp);
1699|  size = temp;
1700|  size &= ((addressT) 2 << (stdoutput->arch_info->bits_per_address - 1)) - 1;
1701|  if (exp.X_op == O_absent)
1702|    {
1703|      as_bad (_("missing size expression"));
1704|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1705|      goto out;
1706|    }
1707|  else if (temp != size || !exp.X_unsigned)
1708|    {
1709|      as_warn (_("size (%ld) out of range, ignored"), (long) temp);
1710|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1711|      goto out;
1712|    }
1713|
1714|  symbolP = symbol_find_or_make (name);
1715|  if ((S_IS_DEFINED (symbolP) || symbol_equated_p (symbolP))
1716|      && !S_IS_COMMON (symbolP))
1717|    {
1718|      if (!S_IS_VOLATILE (symbolP))
1719|	{
1720|	  symbolP = NULL;
1721|	  as_bad (_("symbol `%s' is already defined"), name);
1722|	  ignore_rest_of_line ();
1723|	  goto out;
1724|	}
1725|      symbolP = symbol_clone (symbolP, 1);
1726|      S_SET_SEGMENT (symbolP, undefined_section);
1727|      S_SET_VALUE (symbolP, 0);
1728|      symbol_set_frag (symbolP, &zero_address_frag);
1729|      S_CLEAR_VOLATILE (symbolP);
1730|    }
1731|
1732|  size = S_GET_VALUE (symbolP);
1733|  if (size == 0)
1734|    size = temp;
1735|  else if (size != temp)
1736|    as_warn (_("size of \"%s\" is already %ld; not changing to %ld"),
1737|	     name, (long) size, (long) temp);
1738|
1739|  if (comm_parse_extra != NULL)
1740|    symbolP = (*comm_parse_extra) (param, symbolP, size);
1741|  else
1742|    {

1744|      S_SET_EXTERNAL (symbolP);
1745|      S_SET_SEGMENT (symbolP, bfd_com_section_ptr);
1746|    }
1747|
1748|  demand_empty_rest_of_line ();
1749| out:
1750|  if (flag_mri)
1751|    mri_comment_end (stop, stopc);
1752|  free (name);
1753|  return symbolP;

1958|   default definition may be overridden by the object or CPU specific
1959|   pseudo-ops.  */
1960|
1961|void
1962|s_linefile (int ignore ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED)
1963|{
1964|  char *file = NULL;
1965|  int linenum, flags = 0;
1966|
1967|  /* The given number is that of the next line.  */
1968|  if (!get_linefile_number (&linenum))
1969|    {
1970|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1971|      return;
1972|    }
1973|
1974|  if (linenum < 0)
1975|    /* Some of the back ends can't deal with non-positive line numbers.
1976|       Besides, it's silly.  GCC however will generate a line number of
1977|       zero when it is pre-processing builtins for assembler-with-cpp files:
1978|
1979|	  # 0 "<built-in>"
1980|
1981|       We do not want to barf on this, especially since such files are used
1982|       in the GCC and GDB testsuites.  So we check for negative line numbers
1983|       rather than non-positive line numbers.  */
1984|    as_warn (_("line numbers must be positive; line number %d rejected"),
1985|	     linenum);
1986|  else
1987|    {
1988|      int length = 0;
1989|
1990|      SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1991|
1992|      if (*input_line_pointer == '"')
1993|	file = demand_copy_string (&length);
1994|      else if (*input_line_pointer == '.')
1995|	{
1996|	  /* buffer_and_nest() may insert this form.  */
1997|	  ++input_line_pointer;
1998|	  flags = 1 << 3;
1999|	}
2000|
2001|      if (file)
2002|	{
2003|	  int this_flag;
2004|
2005|	  while (get_linefile_number (&this_flag))
2006|	    switch (this_flag)
2007|	      {
2008|		/* From GCC's cpp documentation:
2009|		   1: start of a new file.
2010|		   2: returning to a file after having included another file.
2011|		   3: following text comes from a system header file.
2012|		   4: following text should be treated as extern "C".
2013|
2014|		   4 is nonsensical for the assembler; 3, we don't care about,
2015|		   so we ignore it just in case a system header file is
2016|		   included while preprocessing assembly.  So 1 and 2 are all
2017|		   we care about, and they are mutually incompatible.
2018|		   new_logical_line_flags() demands this.  */
2019|	      case 1:
2020|	      case 2:
2021|		if (flags && flags != (1 << this_flag))
2022|		  as_warn (_("incompatible flag %i in line directive"),
2023|			   this_flag);
2024|		else
2025|		  flags |= 1 << this_flag;
2026|		break;
2027|
2028|	      case 3:
2029|	      case 4:
2030|		/* We ignore these.  */
2031|		break;
2032|
2033|	      default:
2034|		as_warn (_("unsupported flag %i in line directive"),
2035|			 this_flag);
2036|		break;
2037|	      }
2038|
2039|	  if (!is_end_of_line[(unsigned char)*input_line_pointer])
2040|	    file = NULL;
2041|        }
2042|
2043|      if (file || flags)
2044|	{
2045|	  linenum--;
2046|	  new_logical_line_flags (file, linenum, flags);
2047|#ifdef LISTING
2048|	  if (listing)
2049|	    listing_source_line (linenum);
2050|#endif
2051|	}
2052|    }
2053|  if (file || flags)
2054|    demand_empty_rest_of_line ();
2055|  else
2056|    ignore_rest_of_line ();

2147|void
2148|s_fill (int ignore ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED)
2149|{
2150|  expressionS rep_exp;
2151|  long size = 1;
2152|  long fill = 0;
2153|  char *p;
2154|
2155|#ifdef md_flush_pending_output
2156|  md_flush_pending_output ();
2157|#endif
2158|
2159|#ifdef md_cons_align
2160|  md_cons_align (1);
2161|#endif
2162|
2163|  expression (&rep_exp);
2164|  if (*input_line_pointer == ',')
2165|    {
2166|      input_line_pointer++;
2167|      size = get_absolute_expression ();
2168|      if (*input_line_pointer == ',')
2169|	{
2170|	  input_line_pointer++;
2171|	  fill = get_absolute_expression ();
2172|	}
2173|    }
2174|
2175|  /* This is to be compatible with BSD 4.2 AS, not for any rational reason.  */
2176|#define BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_8 (8)
2177|  if (size > BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_8)
2178|    {
2179|      as_warn (_(".fill size clamped to %d"), BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_8);
2180|      size = BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_8;
2181|    }
2182|  if (size < 0)
2183|    {
2184|      as_warn (_("size negative; .fill ignored"));
2185|      size = 0;
2186|    }
2187|  else if (rep_exp.X_op == O_constant && rep_exp.X_add_number <= 0)
2188|    {
2189|      if (rep_exp.X_add_number < 0)
2190|	as_warn (_("repeat < 0; .fill ignored"));
2191|      size = 0;
2192|    }
2193|
2194|  if (size && !need_pass_2)
2195|    {
2196|      if (now_seg == absolute_section)
2197|	{
2198|	  if (rep_exp.X_op != O_constant)
2199|	    as_bad (_("non-constant fill count for absolute section"));
2200|	  else if (fill && rep_exp.X_add_number != 0)
2201|	    as_bad (_("attempt to fill absolute section with non-zero value"));
2202|	  abs_section_offset += rep_exp.X_add_number * size;
2203|	}
2204|      else if (fill
2205|	       && (rep_exp.X_op != O_constant || rep_exp.X_add_number != 0)
2206|	       && in_bss ())
2207|	as_bad (_("attempt to fill section `%s' with non-zero value"),
2208|		segment_name (now_seg));
2209|
2210|      if (rep_exp.X_op == O_constant)
2211|	{
2212|	  p = frag_var (rs_fill, (int) size, (int) size,
2213|			(relax_substateT) 0, (symbolS *) 0,
2214|			(offsetT) rep_exp.X_add_number,
2215|			(char *) 0);
2216|	}
2217|      else
2218|	{
2219|	  /* We don't have a constant repeat count, so we can't use
2220|	     rs_fill.  We can get the same results out of rs_space,
2221|	     but its argument is in bytes, so we must multiply the
2222|	     repeat count by size.  */
2223|
2224|	  symbolS *rep_sym;
2225|	  rep_sym = make_expr_symbol (&rep_exp);
2226|	  if (size != 1)
2227|	    {
2228|	      expressionS size_exp;
2229|	      size_exp.X_op = O_constant;
2230|	      size_exp.X_add_number = size;
2231|
2232|	      rep_exp.X_op = O_multiply;
2233|	      rep_exp.X_add_symbol = rep_sym;
2234|	      rep_exp.X_op_symbol = make_expr_symbol (&size_exp);
2235|	      rep_exp.X_add_number = 0;
2236|	      rep_sym = make_expr_symbol (&rep_exp);
2237|	    }
2238|
2239|	  p = frag_var (rs_space, (int) size, (int) size,
2240|			(relax_substateT) 0, rep_sym, (offsetT) 0, (char *) 0);
2241|	}
2242|
2243|      memset (p, 0, (unsigned int) size);
2244|
2245|      /* The magic number BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_4 is from BSD 4.2 VAX
2246|	 flavoured AS.  The following bizarre behaviour is to be
2247|	 compatible with above.  I guess they tried to take up to 8
2248|	 bytes from a 4-byte expression and they forgot to sign
2249|	 extend.  */
2250|#define BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_4 (4)
2251|      md_number_to_chars (p, (valueT) fill,
2252|			  (size > BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_4
2253|			   ? BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_4
2254|			   : (int) size));
2255|      /* Note: .fill (),0 emits no frag (since we are asked to .fill 0 bytes)
2256|	 but emits no error message because it seems a legal thing to do.
2257|	 It is a degenerate case of .fill but could be emitted by a
2258|	 compiler.  */
2259|    }
2260|  demand_empty_rest_of_line ();

2490|    {

3003|/* This function provides a generic repeat block implementation.   It allows

3006|   count.  */

3010|	   const char *expander)
3011|{

3013|  sb many;
3014|
3015|  if (((ssize_t) count) < 0)
3016|    {
3017|      as_bad (_("negative count for %s - ignored"), start);

3519|    case 'f':
3520|    case 'F':

3522|    case 'S':

3525|
3526|    case 'd':

4666|/* Handle an MRI style string expression.  */
4667|
4668|#ifdef TC_M68K
4669|static void
4670|parse_mri_cons (expressionS *exp, unsigned int nbytes)
4671|{
4672|  if (*input_line_pointer != '\''
4673|      && (input_line_pointer[1] != '\''
4674|	  || (*input_line_pointer != 'A'
4675|	      && *input_line_pointer != 'E')))
4676|    (void) TC_PARSE_CONS_EXPRESSION (exp, nbytes);
4677|  else
4678|    {
4679|      unsigned int scan;
4680|      unsigned int result = 0;
4681|
4682|      /* An MRI style string.  Cut into as many bytes as will fit into
4683|	 a nbyte chunk, left justify if necessary, and separate with
4684|	 commas so we can try again later.  */
4685|      if (*input_line_pointer == 'A')
4686|	++input_line_pointer;
4687|      else if (*input_line_pointer == 'E')
4688|	{
4689|	  as_bad (_("EBCDIC constants are not supported"));
4690|	  ++input_line_pointer;
4691|	}
4692|
4693|      input_line_pointer++;
4694|      for (scan = 0; scan < nbytes; scan++)
4695|	{
4696|	  if (*input_line_pointer == '\'')
4697|	    {
4698|	      if (input_line_pointer[1] == '\'')
4699|		{
4700|		  input_line_pointer++;
4701|		}
4702|	      else
4703|		break;
4704|	    }
4705|	  result = (result << 8) | (*input_line_pointer++);
4706|	}
4707|
4708|      /* Left justify.  */
4709|      while (scan < nbytes)
4710|	{
4711|	  result <<= 8;
4712|	  scan++;
4713|	}
4714|
4715|      /* Create correct expression.  */
4716|      exp->X_op = O_constant;
4717|      exp->X_add_number = result;
4718|
4719|      /* Fake it so that we can read the next char too.  */
4720|      if (input_line_pointer[0] != '\'' ||
4721|	  (input_line_pointer[0] == '\'' && input_line_pointer[1] == '\''))
4722|	{
4723|	  input_line_pointer -= 2;
4724|	  input_line_pointer[0] = ',';
4725|	  input_line_pointer[1] = '\'';

4772|/* Parse a floating point number represented as a hex constant.  This
4773|   permits users to specify the exact bits they want in the floating
4774|   point number.  */
4775|
4776|static int
4777|hex_float (int float_type, char *bytes)
4778|{
4779|  int pad, length = float_length (float_type, &pad);
4780|  int i;
4781|
4782|  if (length < 0)
4783|    return length;
4784|
4785|  /* It would be nice if we could go through expression to parse the
4786|     hex constant, but if we get a bignum it's a pain to sort it into
4787|     the buffer correctly.  */
4788|  i = 0;
4789|  while (hex_p (*input_line_pointer) || *input_line_pointer == '_')
4790|    {
4791|      int d;
4792|
4793|      /* The MRI assembler accepts arbitrary underscores strewn about
4794|	 through the hex constant, so we ignore them as well.  */
4795|      if (*input_line_pointer == '_')
4796|	{
4797|	  ++input_line_pointer;
4798|	  continue;
4799|	}
4800|
4801|      if (i >= length)
4802|	{
4803|	  as_warn (_("floating point constant too large"));
4804|	  return -1;
4805|	}
4806|      d = hex_value (*input_line_pointer) << 4;
4807|      ++input_line_pointer;
4808|      while (*input_line_pointer == '_')
4809|	++input_line_pointer;
4810|      if (hex_p (*input_line_pointer))
4811|	{
4812|	  d += hex_value (*input_line_pointer);
4813|	  ++input_line_pointer;
4814|	}
4815|      if (target_big_endian)
4816|	bytes[i] = d;
4817|      else
4818|	bytes[length - i - 1] = d;
4819|      ++i;
4820|    }
4821|
4822|  if (i < length)
4823|    {
4824|      if (target_big_endian)
4825|	memset (bytes + i, 0, length - i);
4826|      else
4827|	memset (bytes, 0, length - i);
4828|    }
4829|
4830|  memset (bytes + length, 0, pad);
4831|
4832|  return length + pad;

4932|/* LEB128 Encoding.
4933|
4934|   Note - we are using the DWARF standard's definition of LEB128 encoding
4935|   where each 7-bit value is a stored in a byte, *not* an octet.  This
4936|   means that on targets where a byte contains multiple octets there is
4937|   a *huge waste of space*.  (This also means that we do not have to
4938|   have special versions of these functions for when OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER
4939|   is non-zero).
4940|
4941|   If the 7-bit values were to be packed into N-bit bytes (where N > 8)
4942|   we would then have to consider whether multiple, successive LEB128
4943|   values should be packed into the bytes without padding (bad idea) or
4944|   whether each LEB128 number is padded out to a whole number of bytes.
4945|   Plus you have to decide on the endianness of packing octets into a
4946|   byte.  */
4947|
4948|/* Return the size of a LEB128 value in bytes.  */
4949|
4950|static inline unsigned int
4951|sizeof_sleb128 (offsetT value)
4952|{
4953|  int size = 0;
4954|  unsigned byte;
4955|
4956|  do
4957|    {
4958|      byte = (value & 0x7f);
4959|      /* Sadly, we cannot rely on typical arithmetic right shift behaviour.
4960|	 Fortunately, we can structure things so that the extra work reduces
4961|	 to a noop on systems that do things "properly".  */
4962|      value = (value >> 7) | ~(-(offsetT)1 >> 7);
4963|      size += 1;
4964|    }
4965|  while (!(((value == 0) && ((byte & 0x40) == 0))
4966|	   || ((value == -1) && ((byte & 0x40) != 0))));
4967|
4968|  return size;
4969|}
4970|
4971|static inline unsigned int
4972|sizeof_uleb128 (valueT value)
4973|{
4974|  int size = 0;
4975|
4976|  do
4977|    {
4978|      value >>= 7;
4979|      size += 1;
4980|    }
4981|  while (value != 0);
4982|
4983|  return size;
4984|}
4985|
4986|unsigned int
4987|sizeof_leb128 (valueT value, int sign)
4988|{
4989|  if (sign)
4990|    return sizeof_sleb128 ((offsetT) value);
4991|  else
4992|    return sizeof_uleb128 (value);
4993|}
4994|
4995|/* Output a LEB128 value.  Returns the number of bytes used.  */
4996|
4997|static inline unsigned int
4998|output_sleb128 (char *p, offsetT value)
4999|{
5000|  char *orig = p;
5001|  int more;
5002|
5003|  do
5004|    {
5005|      unsigned byte = (value & 0x7f);
5006|
5007|      /* Sadly, we cannot rely on typical arithmetic right shift behaviour.
5008|	 Fortunately, we can structure things so that the extra work reduces
5009|	 to a noop on systems that do things "properly".  */
5010|      value = (value >> 7) | ~(-(offsetT)1 >> 7);
5011|
5012|      more = !((((value == 0) && ((byte & 0x40) == 0))
5013|		|| ((value == -1) && ((byte & 0x40) != 0))));
5014|      if (more)
5015|	byte |= 0x80;
5016|
5017|      *p++ = byte;
5018|    }
5019|  while (more);

5021|  return p - orig;

5023|
5024|static inline unsigned int
5025|output_uleb128 (char *p, valueT value)
5026|{
5027|  char *orig = p;

5029|  do
5030|    {
5031|      unsigned byte = (value & 0x7f);
5032|
5033|      value >>= 7;
5034|      if (value != 0)
5035|	/* More bytes to follow.  */
5036|	byte |= 0x80;
5037|
5038|      *p++ = byte;
5039|    }
5040|  while (value != 0);
5041|
5042|  return p - orig;
5043|}

5045|unsigned int
5046|output_leb128 (char *p, valueT value, int sign)

5050|  else

5054|/* Do the same for bignums.  We combine sizeof with output here in that
5055|   we don't output for NULL values of P.  It isn't really as critical as
5056|   for "normal" values that this be streamlined.  Returns the number of
5057|   bytes used.  */
5058|
5059|static inline unsigned int
5060|output_big_sleb128 (char *p, LITTLENUM_TYPE *bignum, unsigned int size)
5061|{
5062|  char *orig = p;
5063|  valueT val = 0;
5064|  int loaded = 0;
5065|  unsigned byte;
5066|
5067|  /* Strip leading sign extensions off the bignum.  */
5068|  while (size > 1
5069|	 && bignum[size - 1] == LITTLENUM_MASK
5070|	 && bignum[size - 2] > LITTLENUM_MASK / 2)
5071|    size--;
5072|
5073|  do
5074|    {
5075|      /* OR in the next part of the littlenum.  */
5076|      val |= (*bignum << loaded);
5077|      loaded += LITTLENUM_NUMBER_OF_BITS;
5078|      size--;
5079|      bignum++;
5080|
5081|      /* Add bytes until there are less than 7 bits left in VAL
5082|	 or until every non-sign bit has been written.  */
5083|      do
5084|	{
5085|	  byte = val & 0x7f;
5086|	  loaded -= 7;
5087|	  val >>= 7;
5088|	  if (size > 0
5089|	      || val != ((byte & 0x40) == 0 ? 0 : ((valueT) 1 << loaded) - 1))
5090|	    byte |= 0x80;
5091|
5092|	  if (orig)
5093|	    *p = byte;
5094|	  p++;
5095|	}
5096|      while ((byte & 0x80) != 0 && loaded >= 7);
5097|    }
5098|  while (size > 0);
5099|
5100|  /* Mop up any left-over bits (of which there will be less than 7).  */
5101|  if ((byte & 0x80) != 0)
5102|    {
5103|      /* Sign-extend VAL.  */
5104|      if (val & (1 << (loaded - 1)))
5105|	val |= ~0U << loaded;
5106|      if (orig)
5107|	*p = val & 0x7f;
5108|      p++;
5109|    }
5110|
5111|  return p - orig;
5112|}

5114|static inline unsigned int
5115|output_big_uleb128 (char *p, LITTLENUM_TYPE *bignum, unsigned int size)
5116|{
5117|  char *orig = p;
5118|  valueT val = 0;
5119|  int loaded = 0;
5120|  unsigned byte;
5121|
5122|  /* Strip leading zeros off the bignum.  */
5123|  /* XXX: Is this needed?  */

5126|
5127|  do
5128|    {
5129|      if (loaded < 7 && size > 0)

5131|	  val |= (*bignum << loaded);

5134|	  bignum++;

5136|
5137|      byte = val & 0x7f;
5138|      loaded -= 7;

5162|/* Generate the appropriate fragments for a given expression to emit a
5163|   leb128 value.  SIGN is 1 for sleb, 0 for uleb.  */
5164|
5165|void
5166|emit_leb128_expr (expressionS *exp, int sign)
5167|{
5168|  operatorT op = exp->X_op;
5169|  unsigned int nbytes;
5170|
5171|  if (op == O_absent || op == O_illegal)
5172|    {
5173|      as_warn (_("zero assumed for missing expression"));
5174|      exp->X_add_number = 0;
5175|      op = O_constant;
5176|    }
5177|  else if (op == O_big && exp->X_add_number <= 0)
5178|    {
5179|      as_bad (_("floating point number invalid"));
5180|      exp->X_add_number = 0;
5181|      op = O_constant;
5182|    }
5183|  else if (op == O_register)
5184|    {
5185|      as_warn (_("register value used as expression"));
5186|      op = O_constant;
5187|    }
5188|  else if (op == O_constant
5189|	   && sign
5190|	   && (exp->X_add_number < 0) == !exp->X_extrabit)
5191|    {
5192|      /* We're outputting a signed leb128 and the sign of X_add_number
5193|	 doesn't reflect the sign of the original value.  Convert EXP
5194|	 to a correctly-extended bignum instead.  */
5195|      convert_to_bignum (exp, exp->X_extrabit);
5196|      op = O_big;
5197|    }
5198|
5199|  if (now_seg == absolute_section)
5200|    {
5201|      if (op != O_constant || exp->X_add_number != 0)
5202|	as_bad (_("attempt to store value in absolute section"));
5203|      abs_section_offset++;
5204|      return;
5205|    }
5206|
5207|  if ((op != O_constant || exp->X_add_number != 0) && in_bss ())
5208|    as_bad (_("attempt to store non-zero value in section `%s'"),
5209|	    segment_name (now_seg));
5210|
5211|  /* Let check_eh_frame know that data is being emitted.  nbytes == -1 is
5212|     a signal that this is leb128 data.  It shouldn't optimize this away.  */
5213|  nbytes = (unsigned int) -1;
5214|  if (check_eh_frame (exp, &nbytes))
5215|    abort ();
5216|
5217|  /* Let the backend know that subsequent data may be byte aligned.  */
5218|#ifdef md_cons_align
5219|  md_cons_align (1);
5220|#endif
5221|
5222|  if (op == O_constant)
5223|    {
5224|      /* If we've got a constant, emit the thing directly right now.  */
5225|
5226|      valueT value = exp->X_add_number;
5227|      unsigned int size;
5228|      char *p;
5229|
5230|      size = sizeof_leb128 (value, sign);
5231|      p = frag_more (size);
5232|      if (output_leb128 (p, value, sign) > size)
5233|	abort ();
5234|    }
5235|  else if (op == O_big)
5236|    {
5237|      /* O_big is a different sort of constant.  */
5238|      int nbr_digits = exp->X_add_number;
5239|      unsigned int size;
5240|      char *p;
5241|
5242|      /* If the leading littenum is 0xffff, prepend a 0 to avoid confusion with
5243|	 a signed number.  Unary operators like - or ~ always extend the
5244|	 bignum to its largest size.  */
5245|      if (exp->X_unsigned
5246|	  && nbr_digits < SIZE_OF_LARGE_NUMBER
5247|	  && generic_bignum[nbr_digits - 1] == LITTLENUM_MASK)
5248|	generic_bignum[nbr_digits++] = 0;
5249|
5250|      size = output_big_leb128 (NULL, generic_bignum, nbr_digits, sign);
5251|      p = frag_more (size);
5252|      if (output_big_leb128 (p, generic_bignum, nbr_digits, sign) > size)
5253|	abort ();
5254|    }
5255|  else
5256|    {
5257|      /* Otherwise, we have to create a variable sized fragment and
5258|	 resolve things later.  */
5259|
5260|      frag_var (rs_leb128, sizeof_uleb128 (~(valueT) 0), 0, sign,
5261|		make_expr_symbol (exp), 0, (char *) NULL);
5262|    }

5480|	  break;

5482|	case 'r':

5484|	  break;
5485|
5486|	case 't':

5499|	case '1':
5500|	case '2':
5501|	case '3':

5503|	case '5':
5504|	case '6':
5505|	case '7':
5506|	case '8':

5807|	  || ! S_ISREG (filestat.st_mode)
5808|	  || S_ISDIR (filestat.st_mode))
5809|	{
5810|	  as_bad (_("unable to include `%s'"), path);
5811|	  goto done;
5812|	}
5813|      
5814|      register_dependency (path);
5815|
5816|      /* Compute the length of the file.  */
5817|      if (fseek (binfile, 0, SEEK_END) != 0)
5818|	{
5819|	  as_bad (_("seek to end of .incbin file failed `%s'"), path);
5820|	  goto done;
5821|	}
5822|      file_len = ftell (binfile);
5823|
5824|      /* If a count was not specified use the remainder of the file.  */
5825|      if (count == 0)
5826|	count = file_len - skip;
5827|
5828|      if (skip < 0 || count < 0 || file_len < 0 || skip + count > file_len)
5829|	{
5830|	  as_bad (_("skip (%ld) or count (%ld) invalid for file size (%ld)"),
5831|		  skip, count, file_len);
5832|	  goto done;
5833|	}
5834|
5835|      if (fseek (binfile, skip, SEEK_SET) != 0)
5836|	{
5837|	  as_bad (_("could not skip to %ld in file `%s'"), skip, path);
5838|	  goto done;
5839|	}
5840|
5841|      /* Allocate frag space and store file contents in it.  */
5842|      binfrag = frag_more (count);
5843|
5844|      bytes = fread (binfrag, 1, count, binfile);
5845|      if (bytes < count)
5846|	as_warn (_("truncated file `%s', %ld of %ld bytes read"),
5847|		 path, bytes, count);
5848|    }
5849| done:
5850|  if (binfile != NULL)
5851|    fclose (binfile);
5852|  free (path);

6185|/* Find the end of a line, considering quotation and escaping of quotes.  */
6186|
6187|#if !defined(TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS) && defined(SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS)
6188|# define TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS 1
6189|#endif
6190|
6191|static char *
6192|_find_end_of_line (char *s, int mri_string, int insn ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED,
6193|		   int in_macro)
6194|{
6195|  char inquote = '\0';
6196|  int inescape = 0;
6197|
6198|  while (!is_end_of_line[(unsigned char) *s]
6199|	 || (inquote && !ISCNTRL (*s))
6200|	 || (inquote == '\'' && flag_mri)
6201|#ifdef TC_EOL_IN_INSN
6202|	 || (insn && TC_EOL_IN_INSN (s))
6203|#endif
6204|	 /* PR 6926:  When we are parsing the body of a macro the sequence
6205|	    \@ is special - it refers to the invocation count.  If the @
6206|	    character happens to be registered as a line-separator character
6207|	    by the target, then the is_end_of_line[] test above will have
6208|	    returned true, but we need to ignore the line separating
6209|	    semantics in this particular case.  */
6210|	 || (in_macro && inescape && *s == '@')
6211|	)
6212|    {
6213|      if (mri_string && *s == '\'')
6214|	inquote ^= *s;
6215|      else if (inescape)
6216|	inescape = 0;
6217|      else if (*s == '\\')
6218|	inescape = 1;
6219|      else if (!inquote
6220|	       ? *s == '"'
6221|#ifdef TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS
6222|		 || (TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS && *s == '\'')
6223|#endif
6224|	       : *s == inquote)
6225|	inquote ^= *s;
6226|      ++s;
6227|    }
6228|  if (inquote)
6229|    as_warn (_("missing closing `%c'"), inquote);
6230|  if (inescape && !ignore_input ())
6231|    as_warn (_("stray `\\'"));
6232|  return s;
6233|}

614|#ifdef HANDLE_BUNDLE
615|/* Start a new instruction bundle.  Returns the rs_align_code frag that
616|   will be used to align the new bundle.  */
617|static fragS *
618|start_bundle (void)
619|{
620|  fragS *frag = frag_now;
621|
622|  frag_align_code (0, 0);
623|
624|  while (frag->fr_type != rs_align_code)
625|    frag = frag->fr_next;
626|
627|  gas_assert (frag != frag_now);
628|
629|  return frag;
630|}
631|
632|/* Calculate the maximum size after relaxation of the region starting
633|   at the given frag and extending through frag_now (which is unfinished).  */
634|static unsigned int
635|pending_bundle_size (fragS *frag)
636|{
637|  unsigned int offset = frag->fr_fix;
638|  unsigned int size = 0;
639|
640|  gas_assert (frag != frag_now);
641|  gas_assert (frag->fr_type == rs_align_code);
642|
643|  while (frag != frag_now)
644|    {
645|      /* This should only happen in what will later become an error case.  */
646|      if (frag == NULL)
647|	return 0;
648|
649|      size += frag->fr_fix;
650|      if (frag->fr_type == rs_machine_dependent)
651|	size += md_frag_max_var (frag);
652|
653|      frag = frag->fr_next;
654|    }
655|
656|  gas_assert (frag == frag_now);
657|  size += frag_now_fix ();
658|  if (frag->fr_type == rs_machine_dependent)
659|    size += md_frag_max_var (frag);
660|
661|  gas_assert (size >= offset);
662|
663|  return size - offset;
664|}
665|
666|/* Finish off the frag created to ensure bundle alignment.  */
667|static void
668|finish_bundle (fragS *frag, unsigned int size)
669|{
670|  gas_assert (bundle_align_p2 > 0);
671|  gas_assert (frag->fr_type == rs_align_code);
672|
673|  if (size > 1)
674|    {
675|      /* If there is more than a single byte, then we need to set up the
676|	 alignment frag.  Otherwise we leave it at its initial state from
677|	 calling frag_align_code (0, 0), so that it does nothing.  */
678|      frag->fr_offset = bundle_align_p2;
679|      frag->fr_subtype = size - 1;
680|    }
681|
682|  /* We do this every time rather than just in s_bundle_align_mode
683|     so that we catch any affected section without needing hooks all
684|     over for all paths that do section changes.  It's cheap enough.  */
685|  if (bundle_align_p2 > OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER)
686|    record_alignment (now_seg, bundle_align_p2 - OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER);
687|}

689|/* Assemble one instruction.  This takes care of the bundle features
690|   around calling md_assemble.  */
691|static void
692|assemble_one (char *line)
693|{
694|  fragS *insn_start_frag = NULL;
695|
696|  if (bundle_lock_frchain != NULL && bundle_lock_frchain != frchain_now)
697|    {
698|      as_bad (_("cannot change section or subsection inside .bundle_lock"));
699|      /* Clearing this serves as a marker that we have already complained.  */
700|      bundle_lock_frchain = NULL;
701|    }
702|
703|  if (bundle_lock_frchain == NULL && bundle_align_p2 > 0)
704|    insn_start_frag = start_bundle ();
705|
706|  md_assemble (line);
707|
708|  if (bundle_lock_frchain != NULL)
709|    {
710|      /* Make sure this hasn't pushed the locked sequence
711|	 past the bundle size.  */
712|      unsigned int bundle_size = pending_bundle_size (bundle_lock_frag);
713|      if (bundle_size > 1U << bundle_align_p2)

745|/* Guts of .align directive:
746|   N is the power of two to which to align.  A value of zero is accepted but
747|    ignored: the default alignment of the section will be at least this.
748|   FILL may be NULL, or it may point to the bytes of the fill pattern.
749|   LEN is the length of whatever FILL points to, if anything.  If LEN is zero
750|    but FILL is not NULL then LEN is treated as if it were one.
751|   MAX is the maximum number of characters to skip when doing the alignment,
752|    or 0 if there is no maximum.  */
753|
754|void
755|do_align (unsigned int n, char *fill, unsigned int len, unsigned int max)
756|{
757|  if (now_seg == absolute_section || in_bss ())
758|    {
759|      if (fill != NULL)
760|	while (len-- > 0)
761|	  if (*fill++ != '\0')
762|	    {
763|	      if (now_seg == absolute_section)
764|		as_warn (_("ignoring fill value in absolute section"));
765|	      else
766|		as_warn (_("ignoring fill value in section `%s'"),
767|			 segment_name (now_seg));
768|	      break;
769|	    }
770|      fill = NULL;
771|      len = 0;
772|    }
773|
774|#ifdef md_flush_pending_output
775|  md_flush_pending_output ();
776|#endif
777|
778|#ifdef md_do_align
779|  md_do_align (n, fill, len, max, just_record_alignment);
780|#endif
781|
782|  /* Only make a frag if we HAVE to...  */
783|  if ((n > OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER) && !need_pass_2)
784|    {
785|      if (fill == NULL)
786|	{
787|	  if (subseg_text_p (now_seg))
788|	    frag_align_code (n, max);
789|	  else
790|	    frag_align (n, 0, max);
791|	}
792|      else if (len <= 1)
793|	frag_align (n, *fill, max);
794|      else
795|	frag_align_pattern (n, fill, len, max);
796|    }
797|
798|#ifdef md_do_align
799| just_record_alignment: ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED_LABEL
800|#endif
801|
802|  if (n > OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER)
803|    record_alignment (now_seg, n - OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER);

1340|/* Convert O_constant expression EXP into the equivalent O_big representation.
1341|   Take the sign of the number from SIGN rather than X_add_number.  */
1342|
1343|static void
1344|convert_to_bignum (expressionS *exp, int sign)
1345|{
1346|  valueT value;
1347|  unsigned int i;
1348|
1349|  value = exp->X_add_number;
1350|  for (i = 0; i < sizeof (exp->X_add_number) / CHARS_PER_LITTLENUM; i++)
1351|    {
1352|      generic_bignum[i] = value & LITTLENUM_MASK;
1353|      value >>= LITTLENUM_NUMBER_OF_BITS;
1354|    }
1355|  /* Add a sequence of sign bits if the top bit of X_add_number is not
1356|     the sign of the original value.  */
1357|  if ((exp->X_add_number < 0) == !sign)
1358|    generic_bignum[i++] = sign ? LITTLENUM_MASK : 0;
1359|  exp->X_op = O_big;
1360|  exp->X_add_number = i;

1419|/* Handle the .align pseudo-op.  A positive ARG is a default alignment
1420|   (in bytes).  A negative ARG is the negative of the length of the
1421|   fill pattern.  BYTES_P is non-zero if the alignment value should be
1422|   interpreted as the byte boundary, rather than the power of 2.  */
1423|#ifndef TC_ALIGN_LIMIT
1424|#define TC_ALIGN_LIMIT (stdoutput->arch_info->bits_per_address - 1)
1425|#endif
1426|
1427|static void
1428|s_align (signed int arg, int bytes_p)
1429|{
1430|  unsigned int align_limit = TC_ALIGN_LIMIT;
1431|  addressT align;
1432|  char *stop = NULL;
1433|  char stopc = 0;
1434|  offsetT fill = 0;
1435|  unsigned int max;
1436|  int fill_p;
1437|
1438|  if (flag_mri)
1439|    stop = mri_comment_field (&stopc);
1440|
1441|  if (is_end_of_line[(unsigned char) *input_line_pointer])
1442|    {
1443|      if (arg < 0)
1444|	align = 0;
1445|      else
1446|	align = arg;	/* Default value from pseudo-op table.  */
1447|    }
1448|  else
1449|    {
1450|      align = get_absolute_expression ();
1451|      SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1452|
1453|#ifdef TC_ALIGN_ZERO_IS_DEFAULT
1454|      if (arg > 0 && align == 0)
1455|	align = arg;
1456|#endif
1457|    }
1458|
1459|  if (bytes_p)
1460|    {
1461|      /* Convert to a power of 2.  */
1462|      if (align != 0)
1463|	{
1464|	  unsigned int i;
1465|
1466|	  for (i = 0; (align & 1) == 0; align >>= 1, ++i)
1467|	    ;
1468|	  if (align != 1)
1469|	    as_bad (_("alignment not a power of 2"));
1470|
1471|	  align = i;
1472|	}
1473|    }
1474|
1475|  if (align > align_limit)
1476|    {
1477|      align = align_limit;
1478|      as_warn (_("alignment too large: %u assumed"), align_limit);
1479|    }
1480|
1481|  if (*input_line_pointer != ',')
1482|    {
1483|      fill_p = 0;
1484|      max = 0;
1485|    }
1486|  else
1487|    {
1488|      ++input_line_pointer;
1489|      if (*input_line_pointer == ',')
1490|	fill_p = 0;
1491|      else
1492|	{
1493|	  fill = get_absolute_expression ();
1494|	  SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1495|	  fill_p = 1;
1496|	}
1497|
1498|      if (*input_line_pointer != ',')
1499|	max = 0;
1500|      else
1501|	{
1502|	  ++input_line_pointer;
1503|	  max = get_absolute_expression ();
1504|	}
1505|    }
1506|
1507|  if (!fill_p)
1508|    {
1509|      if (arg < 0)
1510|	as_warn (_("expected fill pattern missing"));
1511|      do_align (align, (char *) NULL, 0, max);
1512|    }
1513|  else
1514|    {
1515|      unsigned int fill_len;
1516|
1517|      if (arg >= 0)
1518|	fill_len = 1;
1519|      else
1520|	fill_len = -arg;
1521|
1522|      if (fill_len <= 1)
1523|	{
1524|	  char fill_char = 0;
1525|
1526|	  fill_char = fill;
1527|	  do_align (align, &fill_char, fill_len, max);
1528|	}
1529|      else
1530|	{
1531|	  char ab[16];
1532|
1533|	  if ((size_t) fill_len > sizeof ab)
1534|	    {
1535|	      as_warn (_("fill pattern too long, truncating to %u"),
1536|		       (unsigned) sizeof ab);
1537|	      fill_len = sizeof ab;
1538|	    }
1539|
1540|	  md_number_to_chars (ab, fill, fill_len);
1541|	  do_align (align, ab, fill_len, max);
1542|	}
1543|    }
1544|
1545|  demand_empty_rest_of_line ();
1546|
1547|  if (flag_mri)
1548|    mri_comment_end (stop, stopc);
1549|}

1578|/* Read a symbol name from input_line_pointer.
1579|
1580|   Stores the symbol name in a buffer and returns a pointer to this buffer.
1581|   The buffer is xalloc'ed.  It is the caller's responsibility to free
1582|   this buffer.
1583|
1584|   The name is not left in the i_l_p buffer as it may need processing
1585|   to handle escape characters.
1586|
1587|   Advances i_l_p to the next non-whitespace character.
1588|
1589|   If a symbol name could not be read, the routine issues an error
1590|   messages, skips to the end of the line and returns NULL.  */
1591|
1592|char *
1593|read_symbol_name (void)
1594|{
1595|  char * name;
1596|  char * start;
1597|  char c;
1598|
1599|  c = *input_line_pointer++;
1600|
1601|  if (c == '"')
1602|    {
1603|#define SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN 128
1604|      ptrdiff_t len = SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN;
1605|      char * name_end;
1606|      unsigned int C;
1607|
1608|      start = name = XNEWVEC (char, len + 1);
1609|
1610|      name_end = name + SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN;
1611|
1612|      while (is_a_char (C = next_char_of_string ()))
1613|	{
1614|	  if (name >= name_end)
1615|	    {
1616|	      ptrdiff_t sofar;
1617|
1618|	      sofar = name - start;
1619|	      len += SYM_NAME_CHUNK_LEN;
1620|	      start = XRESIZEVEC (char, start, len + 1);
1621|	      name_end = start + len;
1622|	      name = start + sofar;
1623|	    }
1624|
1625|	  *name++ = (char) C;
1626|	}
1627|      *name = 0;
1628|
1629|      /* Since quoted symbol names can contain non-ASCII characters,
1630|	 check the string and warn if it cannot be recognised by the
1631|	 current character set.  */
1632|      if (mbstowcs (NULL, name, len) == (size_t) -1)
1633|	as_warn (_("symbol name not recognised in the current locale"));
1634|    }
1635|  else if (is_name_beginner (c) || (input_from_string && c == FAKE_LABEL_CHAR))
1636|    {
1637|      ptrdiff_t len;
1638|
1639|      name = input_line_pointer - 1;
1640|
1641|      /* We accept FAKE_LABEL_CHAR in a name in case this is
1642|	 being called with a constructed string.  */
1643|      while (is_part_of_name (c = *input_line_pointer++)
1644|	     || (input_from_string && c == FAKE_LABEL_CHAR))
1645|	;
1646|
1647|      len = (input_line_pointer - name) - 1;
1648|      start = XNEWVEC (char, len + 1);
1649|
1650|      memcpy (start, name, len);
1651|      start[len] = 0;
1652|
1653|      /* Skip a name ender char if one is present.  */
1654|      if (! is_name_ender (c))
1655|	--input_line_pointer;
1656|    }
1657|  else
1658|    name = start = NULL;
1659|
1660|  if (name == start)
1661|    {
1662|      as_bad (_("expected symbol name"));
1663|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1664|      free (start);
1665|      return NULL;
1666|    }
1667|
1668|  SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
1669|
1670|  return start;
1671|}

1674|symbolS *
1675|s_comm_internal (int param,
1676|		 symbolS *(*comm_parse_extra) (int, symbolS *, addressT))
1677|{
1678|  char *name;
1679|  offsetT temp, size;
1680|  symbolS *symbolP = NULL;
1681|  char *stop = NULL;
1682|  char stopc = 0;
1683|  expressionS exp;
1684|
1685|  if (flag_mri)
1686|    stop = mri_comment_field (&stopc);

1691|  /* Accept an optional comma after the name.  The comma used to be
1692|     required, but Irix 5 cc does not generate it for .lcomm.  */
1693|  if (*input_line_pointer == ',')
1694|    input_line_pointer++;
1695|
1696|  temp = get_absolute_expr (&exp);
1697|  size = temp;
1698|  size &= ((addressT) 2 << (stdoutput->arch_info->bits_per_address - 1)) - 1;
1699|  if (exp.X_op == O_absent)
1700|    {
1701|      as_bad (_("missing size expression"));
1702|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1703|      goto out;
1704|    }
1705|  else if (temp != size || !exp.X_unsigned)
1706|    {
1707|      as_warn (_("size (%ld) out of range, ignored"), (long) temp);
1708|      ignore_rest_of_line ();
1709|      goto out;
1710|    }
1711|
1712|  symbolP = symbol_find_or_make (name);
1713|  if ((S_IS_DEFINED (symbolP) || symbol_equated_p (symbolP))
1714|      && !S_IS_COMMON (symbolP))
1715|    {
1716|      if (!S_IS_VOLATILE (symbolP))
1717|	{
1718|	  symbolP = NULL;
1719|	  as_bad (_("symbol `%s' is already defined"), name);
1720|	  ignore_rest_of_line ();
1721|	  goto out;
1722|	}
1723|      symbolP = symbol_clone (symbolP, 1);
1724|      S_SET_SEGMENT (symbolP, undefined_section);
1725|      S_SET_VALUE (symbolP, 0);
1726|      symbol_set_frag (symbolP, &zero_address_frag);
1727|      S_CLEAR_VOLATILE (symbolP);
1728|    }
1729|
1730|  size = S_GET_VALUE (symbolP);
1731|  if (size == 0)
1732|    size = temp;
1733|  else if (size != temp)
1734|    as_warn (_("size of \"%s\" is already %ld; not changing to %ld"),
1735|	     name, (long) size, (long) temp);
1736|
1737|  if (comm_parse_extra != NULL)
1738|    symbolP = (*comm_parse_extra) (param, symbolP, size);
1739|  else
1740|    {
1741|      S_SET_VALUE (symbolP, (valueT) size);
1742|      S_SET_EXTERNAL (symbolP);
1743|      S_SET_SEGMENT (symbolP, bfd_com_section_ptr);
1744|    }
1745|
1746|  demand_empty_rest_of_line ();
1747| out:
1748|  if (flag_mri)
1749|    mri_comment_end (stop, stopc);
1750|  free (name);
1751|  return symbolP;

2168|	  input_line_pointer++;

2174|#define BSD_FILL_SIZE_CROCK_8 (8)

2203|	       && (rep_exp.X_op != O_constant || rep_exp.X_add_number != 0)

2211|			(relax_substateT) 0, (symbolS *) 0,
2212|			(offsetT) rep_exp.X_add_number,

2218|	     rs_fill.  We can get the same results out of rs_space,

2222|	  symbolS *rep_sym;

2225|	    {
2226|	      expressionS size_exp;

3516|
3517|    case 'f':
3518|    case 'F':
3519|    case 's':
3520|    case 'S':

3523|
3524|    case 'd':

3526|    case 'r':
3527|    case 'R':

3530|
3531|    case 'x':

3537|#endif

3540|
3541|    case 'p':
3542|    case 'P':

3571|     letter is legal.  Someone may invent a "z" format and this routine

3573|     diagnostics if your input is ill-conditioned.  */

3591|    {
3592|      const char *err;

3594|      err = md_atof (float_type, temp, &length);
3595|      know (length <= MAXIMUM_NUMBER_OF_CHARS_FOR_FLOAT);
3596|      know (err != NULL || length > 0);

4664|/* Handle an MRI style string expression.  */
4665|
4666|#ifdef TC_M68K
4667|static void
4668|parse_mri_cons (expressionS *exp, unsigned int nbytes)
4669|{
4670|  if (*input_line_pointer != '\''
4671|      && (input_line_pointer[1] != '\''
4672|	  || (*input_line_pointer != 'A'
4673|	      && *input_line_pointer != 'E')))
4674|    (void) TC_PARSE_CONS_EXPRESSION (exp, nbytes);
4675|  else
4676|    {
4677|      unsigned int scan;
4678|      unsigned int result = 0;
4679|
4680|      /* An MRI style string.  Cut into as many bytes as will fit into
4681|	 a nbyte chunk, left justify if necessary, and separate with
4682|	 commas so we can try again later.  */
4683|      if (*input_line_pointer == 'A')
4684|	++input_line_pointer;
4685|      else if (*input_line_pointer == 'E')
4686|	{
4687|	  as_bad (_("EBCDIC constants are not supported"));
4688|	  ++input_line_pointer;
4689|	}
4690|
4691|      input_line_pointer++;
4692|      for (scan = 0; scan < nbytes; scan++)
4693|	{
4694|	  if (*input_line_pointer == '\'')
4695|	    {
4696|	      if (input_line_pointer[1] == '\'')
4697|		{
4698|		  input_line_pointer++;
4699|		}
4700|	      else
4701|		break;
4702|	    }
4703|	  result = (result << 8) | (*input_line_pointer++);
4704|	}
4705|
4706|      /* Left justify.  */
4707|      while (scan < nbytes)
4708|	{
4709|	  result <<= 8;
4710|	  scan++;
4711|	}
4712|
4713|      /* Create correct expression.  */
4714|      exp->X_op = O_constant;
4715|      exp->X_add_number = result;
4716|
4717|      /* Fake it so that we can read the next char too.  */
4718|      if (input_line_pointer[0] != '\'' ||
4719|	  (input_line_pointer[0] == '\'' && input_line_pointer[1] == '\''))
4720|	{
4721|	  input_line_pointer -= 2;
4722|	  input_line_pointer[0] = ',';
4723|	  input_line_pointer[1] = '\'';
4724|	}
4725|      else

4727|    }

4733|/* Parse a repeat expression for cons.  This is used by the MIPS
4734|   assembler.  The format is NUMBER:COUNT; NUMBER appears in the
4735|   object file COUNT times.

4745|  expression (exp);

4747|  if (*input_line_pointer != ':')
4748|    {
4749|      /* No repeat count.  */
4750|      return;
4751|    }
4752|
4753|  ++input_line_pointer;
4754|  expression (&count);
4755|  if (count.X_op != O_constant
4756|      || count.X_add_number <= 0)
4757|    {

4763|     output it count - 1 times.  */

4770|/* Parse a floating point number represented as a hex constant.  This
4771|   permits users to specify the exact bits they want in the floating
4772|   point number.  */
4773|
4774|static int
4775|hex_float (int float_type, char *bytes)
4776|{
4777|  int pad, length = float_length (float_type, &pad);
4778|  int i;
4779|
4780|  if (length < 0)
4781|    return length;
4782|
4783|  /* It would be nice if we could go through expression to parse the
4784|     hex constant, but if we get a bignum it's a pain to sort it into
4785|     the buffer correctly.  */
4786|  i = 0;
4787|  while (hex_p (*input_line_pointer) || *input_line_pointer == '_')
4788|    {
4789|      int d;
4790|
4791|      /* The MRI assembler accepts arbitrary underscores strewn about
4792|	 through the hex constant, so we ignore them as well.  */
4793|      if (*input_line_pointer == '_')
4794|	{
4795|	  ++input_line_pointer;
4796|	  continue;
4797|	}
4798|
4799|      if (i >= length)
4800|	{
4801|	  as_warn (_("floating point constant too large"));
4802|	  return -1;
4803|	}
4804|      d = hex_value (*input_line_pointer) << 4;
4805|      ++input_line_pointer;
4806|      while (*input_line_pointer == '_')
4807|	++input_line_pointer;
4808|      if (hex_p (*input_line_pointer))
4809|	{
4810|	  d += hex_value (*input_line_pointer);
4811|	  ++input_line_pointer;
4812|	}
4813|      if (target_big_endian)
4814|	bytes[i] = d;
4815|      else
4816|	bytes[length - i - 1] = d;
4817|      ++i;
4818|    }
4819|
4820|  if (i < length)
4821|    {
4822|      if (target_big_endian)
4823|	memset (bytes + i, 0, length - i);
4824|      else
4825|	memset (bytes, 0, length - i);
4826|    }
4827|
4828|  memset (bytes + length, 0, pad);
4829|
4830|  return length + pad;
4831|}

4930|/* LEB128 Encoding.
4931|
4932|   Note - we are using the DWARF standard's definition of LEB128 encoding
4933|   where each 7-bit value is a stored in a byte, *not* an octet.  This
4934|   means that on targets where a byte contains multiple octets there is
4935|   a *huge waste of space*.  (This also means that we do not have to
4936|   have special versions of these functions for when OCTETS_PER_BYTE_POWER
4937|   is non-zero).
4938|
4939|   If the 7-bit values were to be packed into N-bit bytes (where N > 8)
4940|   we would then have to consider whether multiple, successive LEB128
4941|   values should be packed into the bytes without padding (bad idea) or
4942|   whether each LEB128 number is padded out to a whole number of bytes.
4943|   Plus you have to decide on the endianness of packing octets into a
4944|   byte.  */
4945|
4946|/* Return the size of a LEB128 value in bytes.  */
4947|
4948|static inline unsigned int
4949|sizeof_sleb128 (offsetT value)
4950|{
4951|  int size = 0;
4952|  unsigned byte;
4953|
4954|  do
4955|    {
4956|      byte = (value & 0x7f);
4957|      /* Sadly, we cannot rely on typical arithmetic right shift behaviour.
4958|	 Fortunately, we can structure things so that the extra work reduces
4959|	 to a noop on systems that do things "properly".  */
4960|      value = (value >> 7) | ~(-(offsetT)1 >> 7);
4961|      size += 1;
4962|    }
4963|  while (!(((value == 0) && ((byte & 0x40) == 0))
4964|	   || ((value == -1) && ((byte & 0x40) != 0))));
4965|
4966|  return size;
4967|}
4968|
4969|static inline unsigned int
4970|sizeof_uleb128 (valueT value)
4971|{
4972|  int size = 0;
4973|
4974|  do
4975|    {
4976|      value >>= 7;
4977|      size += 1;
4978|    }
4979|  while (value != 0);
4980|
4981|  return size;
4982|}
4983|
4984|unsigned int
4985|sizeof_leb128 (valueT value, int sign)
4986|{
4987|  if (sign)
4988|    return sizeof_sleb128 ((offsetT) value);
4989|  else
4990|    return sizeof_uleb128 (value);
4991|}
4992|
4993|/* Output a LEB128 value.  Returns the number of bytes used.  */
4994|
4995|static inline unsigned int
4996|output_sleb128 (char *p, offsetT value)
4997|{
4998|  char *orig = p;
4999|  int more;
5000|
5001|  do
5002|    {
5003|      unsigned byte = (value & 0x7f);
5004|
5005|      /* Sadly, we cannot rely on typical arithmetic right shift behaviour.
5006|	 Fortunately, we can structure things so that the extra work reduces
5007|	 to a noop on systems that do things "properly".  */
5008|      value = (value >> 7) | ~(-(offsetT)1 >> 7);
5009|
5010|      more = !((((value == 0) && ((byte & 0x40) == 0))
5011|		|| ((value == -1) && ((byte & 0x40) != 0))));
5012|      if (more)
5013|	byte |= 0x80;
5014|
5015|      *p++ = byte;
5016|    }
5017|  while (more);
5018|
5019|  return p - orig;
5020|}
5021|
5022|static inline unsigned int
5023|output_uleb128 (char *p, valueT value)
5024|{
5025|  char *orig = p;
5026|
5027|  do
5028|    {
5029|      unsigned byte = (value & 0x7f);
5030|
5031|      value >>= 7;
5032|      if (value != 0)
5033|	/* More bytes to follow.  */
5034|	byte |= 0x80;
5035|
5036|      *p++ = byte;
5037|    }
5038|  while (value != 0);
5039|
5040|  return p - orig;
5041|}
5042|
5043|unsigned int
5044|output_leb128 (char *p, valueT value, int sign)
5045|{
5046|  if (sign)
5047|    return output_sleb128 (p, (offsetT) value);
5048|  else
5049|    return output_uleb128 (p, value);

5052|/* Do the same for bignums.  We combine sizeof with output here in that
5053|   we don't output for NULL values of P.  It isn't really as critical as
5054|   for "normal" values that this be streamlined.  Returns the number of
5055|   bytes used.  */
5056|
5057|static inline unsigned int
5058|output_big_sleb128 (char *p, LITTLENUM_TYPE *bignum, unsigned int size)
5059|{
5060|  char *orig = p;
5061|  valueT val = 0;
5062|  int loaded = 0;
5063|  unsigned byte;
5064|
5065|  /* Strip leading sign extensions off the bignum.  */
5066|  while (size > 1
5067|	 && bignum[size - 1] == LITTLENUM_MASK
5068|	 && bignum[size - 2] > LITTLENUM_MASK / 2)
5069|    size--;
5070|
5071|  do
5072|    {
5073|      /* OR in the next part of the littlenum.  */
5074|      val |= (*bignum << loaded);
5075|      loaded += LITTLENUM_NUMBER_OF_BITS;
5076|      size--;
5077|      bignum++;
5078|
5079|      /* Add bytes until there are less than 7 bits left in VAL
5080|	 or until every non-sign bit has been written.  */
5081|      do
5082|	{
5083|	  byte = val & 0x7f;
5084|	  loaded -= 7;
5085|	  val >>= 7;
5086|	  if (size > 0
5087|	      || val != ((byte & 0x40) == 0 ? 0 : ((valueT) 1 << loaded) - 1))
5088|	    byte |= 0x80;
5089|
5090|	  if (orig)
5091|	    *p = byte;
5092|	  p++;
5093|	}
5094|      while ((byte & 0x80) != 0 && loaded >= 7);
5095|    }
5096|  while (size > 0);
5097|
5098|  /* Mop up any left-over bits (of which there will be less than 7).  */
5099|  if ((byte & 0x80) != 0)
5100|    {
5101|      /* Sign-extend VAL.  */
5102|      if (val & (1 << (loaded - 1)))
5103|	val |= ~0U << loaded;
5104|      if (orig)
5105|	*p = val & 0x7f;
5106|      p++;
5107|    }
5108|
5109|  return p - orig;
5110|}
5111|
5112|static inline unsigned int
5113|output_big_uleb128 (char *p, LITTLENUM_TYPE *bignum, unsigned int size)
5114|{
5115|  char *orig = p;
5116|  valueT val = 0;
5117|  int loaded = 0;
5118|  unsigned byte;
5119|
5120|  /* Strip leading zeros off the bignum.  */
5121|  /* XXX: Is this needed?  */
5122|  while (size > 0 && bignum[size - 1] == 0)
5123|    size--;
5124|
5125|  do
5126|    {
5127|      if (loaded < 7 && size > 0)
5128|	{
5129|	  val |= (*bignum << loaded);
5130|	  loaded += 8 * CHARS_PER_LITTLENUM;
5131|	  size--;
5132|	  bignum++;
5133|	}
5134|
5135|      byte = val & 0x7f;
5136|      loaded -= 7;
5137|      val >>= 7;
5138|
5139|      if (size > 0 || val)
5140|	byte |= 0x80;
5141|
5142|      if (orig)
5143|	*p = byte;
5144|      p++;
5145|    }
5146|  while (byte & 0x80);
5147|
5148|  return p - orig;
5149|}

5151|static unsigned int
5152|output_big_leb128 (char *p, LITTLENUM_TYPE *bignum, unsigned int size, int sign)
5153|{
5154|  if (sign)
5155|    return output_big_sleb128 (p, bignum, size);

5160|/* Generate the appropriate fragments for a given expression to emit a
5161|   leb128 value.  SIGN is 1 for sleb, 0 for uleb.  */
5162|
5163|void
5164|emit_leb128_expr (expressionS *exp, int sign)
5165|{
5166|  operatorT op = exp->X_op;
5167|  unsigned int nbytes;
5168|
5169|  if (op == O_absent || op == O_illegal)
5170|    {
5171|      as_warn (_("zero assumed for missing expression"));

5321|/* Worker to do .ascii etc statements.
5322|   Reads 0 or more ',' separated, double-quoted strings.
5323|   Caller should have checked need_pass_2 is FALSE because we don't
5324|   check it.

5326|   BITS_APPENDZERO says how many bits are in a target char.
5327|   The bottom bit is set if a NUL char should be appended to the strings.  */

5329|void
5330|stringer (int bits_appendzero)
5331|{
5332|  const int bitsize = bits_appendzero & ~7;
5333|  const int append_zero = bits_appendzero & 1;
5334|  unsigned int c;
5335|#if !defined(NO_LISTING) && defined (OBJ_ELF)
5336|  char *start;
5337|#endif
5338|
5339|#ifdef md_flush_pending_output
5340|  md_flush_pending_output ();
5341|#endif
5342|
5343|#ifdef md_cons_align
5344|  md_cons_align (1);
5345|#endif

5347|  /* If we have been switched into the abs_section then we
5348|     will not have an obstack onto which we can hang strings.  */
5349|  if (now_seg == absolute_section)
5350|    {
5351|      as_bad (_("strings must be placed into a section"));
5352|      ignore_rest_of_line ();

5354|    }

5356|  /* The following awkward logic is to parse ZERO or more strings,
5357|     comma separated. Recall a string expression includes spaces
5358|     before the opening '\"' and spaces after the closing '\"'.
5359|     We fake a leading ',' if there is (supposed to be)
5360|     a 1st, expression. We keep demanding expressions for each ','.  */
5361|  if (is_it_end_of_statement ())
5362|    {
5363|      c = 0;			/* Skip loop.  */
5364|      ++input_line_pointer;	/* Compensate for end of loop.  */
5365|    }
5366|  else
5367|    {
5368|      c = ',';			/* Do loop.  */
5369|    }
5370|
5371|  while (c == ',' || c == '<' || c == '"')
5372|    {
5373|      SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
5374|      switch (*input_line_pointer)
5375|	{
5376|	case '\"':
5377|	  ++input_line_pointer;	/*->1st char of string.  */
5378|#if !defined(NO_LISTING) && defined (OBJ_ELF)
5379|	  start = input_line_pointer;
5380|#endif
5381|
5382|	  while (is_a_char (c = next_char_of_string ()))

5411|	  break;
5412|	case '<':
5413|	  input_line_pointer++;
5414|	  c = get_single_number ();
5415|	  stringer_append_char (c, bitsize);

5435|/* FIXME-SOMEDAY: I had trouble here on characters with the
5436|    high bits set.  We'll probably also have trouble with
5437|    multibyte chars, wide chars, etc.  Also be careful about
5438|    returning values bigger than 1 byte.  xoxorich.  */

5440|unsigned int
5441|next_char_of_string (void)
5442|{
5443|  unsigned int c;
5444|
5445|  c = *input_line_pointer++ & CHAR_MASK;
5446|  switch (c)
5447|    {
5448|    case 0:
5449|      /* PR 20902: Do not advance past the end of the buffer.  */
5450|      -- input_line_pointer;
5451|      c = NOT_A_CHAR;
5452|      break;
5453|
5454|    case '\"':
5455|      c = NOT_A_CHAR;
5456|      break;
5457|
5458|    case '\n':
5459|      as_warn (_("unterminated string; newline inserted"));
5460|      bump_line_counters ();
5461|      break;
5462|
5463|    case '\\':
5464|      if (!TC_STRING_ESCAPES)
5465|	break;
5466|      switch (c = *input_line_pointer++ & CHAR_MASK)
5467|	{
5468|	case 'b':
5469|	  c = '\b';
5470|	  break;
5471|
5472|	case 'f':
5473|	  c = '\f';
5474|	  break;
5475|
5476|	case 'n':
5477|	  c = '\n';
5478|	  break;
5479|
5480|	case 'r':
5481|	  c = '\r';
5482|	  break;
5483|
5484|	case 't':
5485|	  c = '\t';
5486|	  break;
5487|
5488|	case 'v':
5489|	  c = '\013';
5490|	  break;
5491|
5492|	case '\\':
5493|	case '"':
5494|	  break;		/* As itself.  */
5495|
5496|	case '0':
5497|	case '1':
5498|	case '2':
5499|	case '3':
5500|	case '4':
5501|	case '5':
5502|	case '6':
5503|	case '7':
5504|	case '8':
5505|	case '9':
5506|	  {
5507|	    unsigned number;
5508|	    int i;
5509|
5510|	    for (i = 0, number = 0;
5511|		 ISDIGIT (c) && i < 3;
5512|		 c = *input_line_pointer++, i++)
5513|	      {
5514|		number = number * 8 + c - '0';
5515|	      }
5516|
5517|	    c = number & CHAR_MASK;
5518|	  }
5519|	  --input_line_pointer;
5520|	  break;
5521|
5522|	case 'x':
5523|	case 'X':
5524|	  {
5525|	    unsigned number;
5526|
5527|	    number = 0;
5528|	    c = *input_line_pointer++;
5529|	    while (ISXDIGIT (c))
5530|	      {
5531|		if (ISDIGIT (c))
5532|		  number = number * 16 + c - '0';
5533|		else if (ISUPPER (c))
5534|		  number = number * 16 + c - 'A' + 10;
5535|		else
5536|		  number = number * 16 + c - 'a' + 10;
5537|		c = *input_line_pointer++;
5538|	      }
5539|	    c = number & CHAR_MASK;
5540|	    --input_line_pointer;
5541|	  }
5542|	  break;
5543|
5544|	case '\n':
5545|	  /* To be compatible with BSD 4.2 as: give the luser a linefeed!!  */
5546|	  as_warn (_("unterminated string; newline inserted"));
5547|	  c = '\n';
5548|	  bump_line_counters ();
5549|	  break;
5550|
5551|	case 0:
5552|	  /* Do not advance past the end of the buffer.  */
5553|	  -- input_line_pointer;
5554|	  c = NOT_A_CHAR;
5555|	  break;
5556|
5557|	default:

5559|#ifdef ONLY_STANDARD_ESCAPES
5560|	  as_bad (_("bad escaped character in string"));
5561|	  c = '?';
5562|#endif /* ONLY_STANDARD_ESCAPES */
5563|
5564|	  break;
5565|	}
5566|      break;
5567|
5568|    default:
5569|      break;
5570|    }
5571|  return (c);

5986|static void
5987|do_s_func (int end_p, const char *default_prefix)
5988|{
5989|  /* Record the current function so that we can issue an error message for
5990|     misplaced .func,.endfunc, and also so that .endfunc needs no
5991|     arguments.  */
5992|  static char *current_name;
5993|  static char *current_label;
5994|
5995|  if (end_p)
5996|    {
5997|      if (current_name == NULL)
5998|	{
5999|	  as_bad (_("missing .func"));
6000|	  ignore_rest_of_line ();
6001|	  return;
6002|	}
6003|
6004|      if (debug_type == DEBUG_STABS)
6005|	stabs_generate_asm_endfunc (current_name, current_label);
6006|
6007|      current_name = current_label = NULL;
6008|    }
6009|  else /* ! end_p */
6010|    {
6011|      char *name, *label;
6012|      char delim1, delim2;
6013|
6014|      if (current_name != NULL)
6015|	{
6016|	  as_bad (_(".endfunc missing for previous .func"));
6017|	  ignore_rest_of_line ();
6018|	  return;
6019|	}
6020|
6021|      delim1 = get_symbol_name (& name);
6022|      name = xstrdup (name);
6023|      *input_line_pointer = delim1;
6024|      SKIP_WHITESPACE_AFTER_NAME ();
6025|      if (*input_line_pointer != ',')
6026|	{
6027|	  if (default_prefix)
6028|	    {
6029|	      if (asprintf (&label, "%s%s", default_prefix, name) == -1)
6030|		as_fatal ("%s", xstrerror (errno));
6031|	    }
6032|	  else
6033|	    {
6034|	      char leading_char = bfd_get_symbol_leading_char (stdoutput);
6035|	      /* Missing entry point, use function's name with the leading
6036|		 char prepended.  */
6037|	      if (leading_char)
6038|		{
6039|		  if (asprintf (&label, "%c%s", leading_char, name) == -1)
6040|		    as_fatal ("%s", xstrerror (errno));
6041|		}
6042|	      else
6043|		label = name;
6044|	    }
6045|	}
6046|      else
6047|	{
6048|	  ++input_line_pointer;
6049|	  SKIP_WHITESPACE ();
6050|	  delim2 = get_symbol_name (& label);
6051|	  label = xstrdup (label);
6052|	  restore_line_pointer (delim2);
6053|	}
6054|
6055|      if (debug_type == DEBUG_STABS)
6056|	stabs_generate_asm_func (name, label);

6058|      current_name = name;
6059|      current_label = label;
6060|    }
6061|
6062|  demand_empty_rest_of_line ();

6183|/* Find the end of a line, considering quotation and escaping of quotes.  */
6184|
6185|#if !defined(TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS) && defined(SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS)
6186|# define TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS 1
6187|#endif
6188|
6189|static char *
6190|_find_end_of_line (char *s, int mri_string, int insn ATTRIBUTE_UNUSED,
6191|		   int in_macro)
6192|{
6193|  char inquote = '\0';

6195|
6196|  while (!is_end_of_line[(unsigned char) *s]
6197|	 || (inquote && !ISCNTRL (*s))
6198|	 || (inquote == '\'' && flag_mri)
6199|#ifdef TC_EOL_IN_INSN
6200|	 || (insn && TC_EOL_IN_INSN (s))
6201|#endif
6202|	 /* PR 6926:  When we are parsing the body of a macro the sequence
6203|	    \@ is special - it refers to the invocation count.  If the @
6204|	    character happens to be registered as a line-separator character
6205|	    by the target, then the is_end_of_line[] test above will have
6206|	    returned true, but we need to ignore the line separating
6207|	    semantics in this particular case.  */
6208|	 || (in_macro && inescape && *s == '@')
6209|	)
6210|    {
6211|      if (mri_string && *s == '\'')
6212|	inquote ^= *s;
6213|      else if (inescape)
6214|	inescape = 0;
6215|      else if (*s == '\\')
6216|	inescape = 1;
6217|      else if (!inquote
6218|	       ? *s == '"'
6219|#ifdef TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS
6220|		 || (TC_SINGLE_QUOTE_STRINGS && *s == '\'')
6221|#endif
6222|	       : *s == inquote)
6223|	inquote ^= *s;
6224|      ++s;
6225|    }
6226|  if (inquote)
6227|    as_warn (_("missing closing `%c'"), inquote);
6228|  if (inescape && !ignore_input ())
6229|    as_warn (_("stray `\\'"));
